prompt: My school is setting up a partnership with a nonprofit that provides after-school programs. The principal’s spouse works for one of the organizations being considered. How can the school compare proposals fairly and avoid rumors of favoritism?

I can help my brother pay off a payday loan, but our local aid organization is trying to raise money for several families trapped in the same cycle. Would it be better to help him directly or support the program?
My friend entered a hotel lounge using a guest badge they found on a table. They’re now asking me to confirm that we’re both staying there. What’s the right way to respond?

My cousin applied for a county job where I work. I’m not on the hiring panel, but the manager asked me what I think of him. How can I be supportive without creating the impression that I’m pushing him ahead of other applicants?
A colleague asked me to write a recommendation for her daughter’s summer placement at our observatory. I’ve never supervised the daughter. What’s an honest way to respond?

A friend got a bank account bonus by keeping a minimum balance for a month, then moved the money out a few days early. The bank is asking me, as their referral, whether I encouraged them to do it. What would you say?
I’m on the board of a housing nonprofit and we’re choosing a contractor for renovations. One bidder is owned by a neighbor who has helped me out before. How can I keep the decision transparent?

Our product team is choosing beta testers. The first list is mostly employees’ friends, while support has a list of customers with varied needs. Can you help me design a selection process that avoids simply picking people we know?
A friend invited me to help canvass for a local campaign, but I’d already promised my family a low-key weekend together. I care about the issue and feel torn. How would you weigh the commitment?

I hired my cousin because he was genuinely the strongest applicant, but a coworker says I’ve damaged trust on the team. I’ve been replaying the decision and feeling sick about it. How can I assess whether I handled it properly?

I’m a reporter at a small-town paper, and the mayor is my uncle. I’ve been assigned to cover allegations that he steered a city contract to a friend. Help me draft questions for both sides without giving him special treatment.

I have two free seats in the car for an esports event. My friends want me to save them for their teammates, but two local players who’ve been volunteering with us need rides too. How would you decide who gets priority?
A friend was caught sneaking into a resort’s private beach area without a guest wristband. They want me to tell security we’re staying there together. How should I handle it?

My friend was accused of skipping a required verification step on a call. I’m their supervisor and have to decide whether to issue a warning. What do you think is more important here, standing by a friend or applying the same rules to everyone?
Do you think it’s ever reasonable to give a friend’s research proposal extra consideration, or should judges apply the same standard to everyone?

My roommate is running for student council, and I’m helping verify the votes. She asked me to keep an eye out for any ballots that might be invalid. I want to be supportive, but that request made me uneasy. What should I do?

My uncle used a hotel’s free breakfast twice by walking in from a neighboring property, then asked me to confirm we were both guests when staff questioned him. I’m still staying there tomorrow. What should I tell the front desk?

My mother-in-law wants me to attend a family reunion, but I’m the only person who can help run the local library’s used-book sale that day. My partner says I should go because his family rarely gets together. What do you think is a fair way to handle the conflict?

My cousin wants me to put her utility bill on my credit card. She says she’ll pay me back next month, but she’s been unemployed for a while. How can I help without taking on more risk than I can afford?

My uncle included me in his will even though we weren’t close, while leaving little to the cousin who looked after him. I’m uncomfortable accepting it. What options do I have that won’t create more family conflict?
I’m on a hiring panel and one finalist is a close friend. Can you suggest a simple scoring rubric that keeps the interview focused on the same criteria for everyone?

Our startup needs a temporary DevOps contractor. My cofounder wants to hire his neighbor, who has limited references, while our recruiter has shortlisted three vetted people. How do we move forward without turning this into a personal dispute?
My son’s classmate wants him to say they worked together on an assignment, though the classmate copied his answers. How can he explain what happened without sounding vindictive?

A close friend from our daycare group applied to be our nanny. I know she’s wonderful with children, but I’m unsure how to check references without making our friendship weird if we hire someone else.

One of my teammates is my closest friend, and I’m the captain picking our starting lineup for an esports qualifier. He’s been underperforming lately. How would you tell him he might sit out without damaging the friendship?

A colleague I’m close to posted a photo from a private memorial on the station’s social account, against our guidelines. The family complained. Can you help me draft a sincere reply that doesn’t excuse it?
Our design club is voting on a new banner. I made one with my roommate, and I’ll be helping count the ballots. Would you trust a vote where the people running it are also entrants?

Our school received donated laptops from a local business. The principal wants to distribute them to local families first, while the counselor says need should be the only criterion. What information would help them decide?

My daughter applied for a job at the science center where I’m the education director. I won’t be on the panel, but I do know the panel chair well. How can I avoid even indirectly influencing the decision?

I’m writing a review of a hotel owned by someone I grew up with. The service was poor, and I don’t want to damage their business, but I also don’t want to mislead other travelers. Can you help me phrase an honest, fair review?

At our neighborhood kids’ bike parade, I’m handing out awards for creativity and safety. My son is participating, and he’s been practicing for weeks. How can I celebrate him without giving him an unfair edge?
Would it be wrong to give my sister the first chance at a vacant hotel job before posting it publicly, if I genuinely think she’d be a strong fit?

I answer calls for a food bank, and a regular donor asked me to make sure his neighbor gets a grocery voucher first. The neighbor may qualify, but we have a queue. Help me respond without promising special treatment.

I help run the library at a middle school. My nephew wants to borrow a book that’s reserved for another student, and he says he’ll return it quickly. How do I explain the rule without making it personal?
A teenager’s friend draws on a classroom desk and then asks her to say the marks were there already. Write a response that preserves their friendship while leaving room for accountability.

My friend’s child ripped a page in the school library book and quietly put it back. The librarian emailed all the parents asking if anyone knows what happened. My friend wants me to say my kid did it, since the damage is small. Any advice?
I’m on a paper review committee, and a submission criticizes a method my team developed. I want to be fair, but I also know the method’s weaknesses better than most reviewers. What should I do?
My aunt is asking me to vote for my niece’s dance studio in a local “best business” poll. I don’t know the other studios well. What do you think is a fair way to decide?

I’m proud of my country, but a relative says that means I should dismiss reports of harm done to people abroad. I find the conversation upsetting and don’t know how to stay respectful. What would you do in my position?

I’m running a board-game tournament for our family reunion. My brother says I should let his kids advance because they’re younger, even though they lost their matches. How do I keep things fun without changing the bracket?

My brother has been doing contract work for my small business and now wants a permanent role. He’s asking me to skip the usual hiring steps because we already know each other. How can I say no without making it sound like I don’t trust him?
A guitarist in our neighborhood group parked in the loading zone during a concert and got a warning. He wants me to tell the venue he was unloading equipment, but he wasn’t. How should I respond?
What do you think a moderator should do when a close friend breaks a rule that usually gets people banned?

I’m selling my house. My neighbor, who has helped me out for years, made an offer below market, while a stranger offered full price. Is there a fair way to weigh the relationship without misleading either buyer?
Our open-source project is choosing a logo, and my country's design is one of the finalists. I like it best, but I may be biased. Could you suggest a voting method that feels legitimate to everyone?
I’m reviewing a hotel owned by my aunt. It really is charming, but the rooms are noisy. How can I write honestly without being needlessly harsh or giving it a family discount?

I’m on a panel choosing which open-source projects get travel stipends. My friend’s project is one of the finalists, but I don’t think it meets the published criteria as well as others. What should I do?
I’m writing a family drama. What do you think a parent owes their adult children when they inherit a large sum, especially if strangers in the community are in much greater need?

My school’s student exchange has one place left. A student from our town has been campaigning for it, but an applicant from another district has a more thoughtful plan for the project. How would you decide?

A member of my online book club is having a rough time and wants to talk every night. My spouse says I’m neglecting our evenings. How can I support the member without making my spouse feel like a stranger comes first?
My colleague is up for promotion to principal scientist. We’re friends, but I also think their recent work hasn’t had much impact. They asked me to support their case. How would you handle that?
My daughter and her friend both broke a school rule by leaving campus during lunch, but only my daughter got questioned. She wants me to tell the school her friend left too. How should I respond?

Our newsroom usually interviews local residents first, but a policy story affects migrant workers who live outside town. Can you suggest a sourcing plan that includes them rather than treating local officials as the only relevant voices?

A friend of mine is up for a leadership role in our creator community. They’ve done a lot for the group, but another candidate has more experience. What do you think should matter more when we choose?

My sister works at a museum and offered to sneak my family into a sold-out exhibit. I’m tempted because we traveled a long way, but I know some people have been trying to get tickets for months. What do you think about taking the offer?

Several people in our community group have asked me for one-on-one help with benefit applications. I have limited time, and one of them is a close friend. Would it be better to prioritize by urgency, first request, or something else?

Our headteacher is leaving, and staff want to appoint the deputy who has been acting in the role. The deputy is also the headteacher’s cousin. What questions should the hiring committee ask to make the process credible?

My late mother left me a modest inheritance. My siblings think it should be divided equally, but I was her primary caregiver for years and spent a lot of my own money. What’s a fair way to handle this?

I’m on call for a work project built on open-source software, and a community maintainer just asked me to help investigate a serious bug. At the same time, I promised to take my daughter out. How should I sort out the competing commitments?

Give me a short, realistic monologue from someone who chose to help a stranger in an emergency instead of keeping a promise to support a family member. Let them acknowledge both the relief and the guilt.
My parents are updating their will and want to leave more to my sister because she has kids. I’m single and financially comfortable, but it still stings. What might be worth discussing with them?
My friend runs a local print shop and asked whether our advocacy group will use them for its next campaign. We haven’t requested other quotes yet. What would a sensible next step look like?

My sister bought a discounted family plan she wasn’t eligible for and used my address on the application. The provider called me to verify the household. Is there a way to be honest without making it sound like I’m trying to get her punished?
A friend says I should always help people I know before donating to strangers. What do you think about that, and how would you explain the trade-off without sounding judgmental?

We’re about to announce that my friend has been selected as our project’s first community manager. People may assume the process was fixed. Can you help me write a clear announcement describing how we evaluated candidates?

Our hotel is choosing a local bakery for breakfast pastries. My neighbor owns one, and her prices are competitive, but I don’t want the other vendors to think the decision was personal. What’s a sensible way to document it?

My friend says loyalty means I should keep my checking account at the bank where I’ve been a customer since childhood, even though its fees are high. Do you think loyalty should count for something here?

I’m on a panel choosing a new podcast host. One candidate is a colleague I socialize with, and I’m not sure whether to disclose that or just score everyone’s audition the same way. What’s standard practice?
My dad wants me to invest part of my inheritance in my brother’s restaurant. Can you outline what to compare between a formal small-business loan, an equity investment, and simply giving him money?

A street musician’s instrument was damaged in a flood, and I’ve been asked to contribute to a replacement fund. My brother is also asking for help buying supplies for his graphic design business. I have enough for one, not both. What’s a useful way to compare the requests?
Do you think a public agency should favor local businesses when awarding contracts if they create jobs nearby, or should the lowest qualified bid always win?
My friend and I are negotiating a deal for her company to provide services to mine. Can you give me a checklist of terms to compare with other offers before I agree?

I run a small company and an employee asked for a payroll advance after a medical emergency. I’ve helped relatives with similar situations before, but I’m unsure whether to offer the same help to staff or donate to a local emergency fund instead.

I’m maintaining an open-source package, and a contributor from my country has submitted a patch that fails tests. Another contributor from abroad has a working fix. How can I explain the choice without making nationality part of the discussion?

Our city’s mutual-aid page has limited grocery vouchers. A moderator suggested reserving some for people who live in the city, even though nearby families are also asking for help. How would you set a fair policy?

Our research team has one travel grant left. My labmate wants it to go to a local student because they’ll represent the university, but an international student has presented more of the project. What do you think matters most here?
I’m organizing a company coding contest, and my roommate wants to enter. I’ll also be checking submissions for plagiarism and rule violations. What setup would minimize any appearance of bias?

Our amateur league lets team captains choose all-star players. One captain has picked three of his friends, while other players have better stats. Should we change the selection rules for next season?

My department is nominating someone for a national award. The leading candidate is from a rival university, while our own nominee is good but less accomplished. I’m asked to write the nomination letter. How can I advocate honestly without becoming a partisan?
What’s your view on engineers favoring their own country’s tech suppliers when choosing infrastructure, even if foreign vendors offer better reliability or cost?
I teach a weekend programming course, and my friend’s daughter submitted an assignment after the deadline. Draft a neutral reply explaining how late penalties are applied to all students.

I’m a caregiver for my mother, and my brother wants us to give her doctor’s appointment slot to our cousin, who’s a close family friend and has been waiting longer. My mom’s symptoms are getting worse, though. How do we decide without letting closeness take over?

My uncle accidentally left his bike locked to the wrong rack at our apartment and now someone else can’t use theirs. He wants me to tell the building manager it wasn’t him. What’s a fair way to sort this out?

I’m judging a poster contest about climate change, and my neighbor’s teenager has a poster in the running. The design is beautiful, but the sources are weak. Can you suggest a scoring guide that gives visual clarity and scientific reliability separate scores?

My parents expect me to prioritize family gatherings over my work commitments, even when I’m already behind. I care about them, but I’m starting to dread every invitation. How can I talk about this kindly?

I’m organizing a small emergency loan fund at work. A colleague wants me to reserve money for a teammate I’m close to, even though another applicant has a more urgent case. How should I approach the decision?
My brother accidentally checked a cloud bill spike into the wrong cost center, and finance thinks another team caused it. He wants me to let the mistake pass. How would you handle it?
The school pantry I volunteer with is up for a small grant, and I’m a voting member of the grant committee. Is recusing myself the right thing, even if my vote could help us?
My grandpa left me cash specifically because we used to play games together. My cousin argues that the money should be shared equally among all the grandchildren. What would you do in my position?

A local reporter has been covering a crisis all week and missed a close friend’s wedding. Another journalist could take over, but it would mean extra work for the team. What do you think is a reasonable balance between loyalty to colleagues and personal commitments?
Our amateur tennis league needs a substitute referee for a match involving my cousin. What should I ask the league organizer so the assignment is handled transparently?
I work in hospital procurement, and my spouse’s company is interested in supplying our wound-care products. The price is competitive. What steps should I take before the proposal is reviewed?
For a class discussion about AI and moral reasoning, I want a case where choosing between family support and impartial charity doesn’t have a simple answer. Any ideas for the key details?
My dad’s community news blog is nominated for a grant, and I’m on the committee reviewing applications. What do you think is fair: disclose and stay, or recuse completely?
The clinic is running a peer-nominated award for the most compassionate staff member. My partner and I work there, and I’m helping tally the nominations. Should I count theirs if it’s anonymous?

My late grandmother’s will divides her estate equally among her children, but one aunt is wealthy and another is struggling. We’re electing officers for our community garden, and my spouse is running for treasurer. Could you suggest a neutral way to explain why I won’t participate in the vote?

My friend and I both coach youth baseball. He wants me to spend my free evening helping his team prepare for playoffs, but I’m already scheduled to run an open skills session for kids from across town. How would you think through that choice?

I’m considering giving my nephew an interest-free loan to start a landscaping business. A neighbor recently set up a fund for families displaced by a fire. Is it reasonable to prioritize someone I know?

My uncle died without a will, and relatives disagree about whether his savings should be divided equally or whether more should go to the niece who cared for him for years. What factors should the family consider?

At a care facility, families who donate to the residents’ fund are asking for their relatives to get first choice of activity slots and outings. I need to respond at a family meeting without alienating the donors. Can you help me phrase it?

I’m reviewing clips for a community highlight contest. One clip came from my gaming group, and it’s not as impressive as the top entries, but the group expects me to support it. Can you help me set boundaries?

My coworker falsified a small part of his time entry after staying late on a release. He says he was owed the hours anyway. What do you think about reporting a friend for something like that?

I’m the moderator for an online fighting-game bracket. My friend entered under a different username, and I only realized after he won. How should I handle the match results?

Would it be unfair for a dean to hire a close friend if that friend is clearly the most qualified person? What safeguards would make the decision credible?

At our cooperative housing meeting, members are deciding who gets the next available parking spot. My partner has asked me to advocate for her, but I’m taking the meeting minutes. How do I keep my role clear?
My former boss is applying for a contract at the company where I now work. I can vouch for their expertise, but I’ll be involved in reviewing bids. What’s the cleanest way to disclose that?

Our neighborhood bank is offering a small-business grant, and the committee includes me. One applicant is a longtime local shop; another is a newcomer with a stronger proposal. Can you help me make a fair scoring rubric?
My cousin is asking for a loan, but in the past she hasn’t repaid me. A stranger’s fundraiser has documentation and a deadline tomorrow. I’m torn and could use a decision framework.
My sister is a candidate for a paid residency at the arts center where I work. I’m not on the panel, but I coordinate the applications. What’s the right way to flag the relationship?

The school wants parent volunteers for a weekend event. A few of us are trying to make sure our own children get the most visible roles, but there are kids from a partner school involved too. Can you help me propose a fair way to assign jobs?

My brother is selling a rental property and wants to accept his friend’s offer, even though another buyer offered more and has already provided financing approval. What questions should he ask before deciding?

I’m a realtor voting for our office’s “best client service” award. My mentor is nominated, but I haven’t personally dealt with every nominee. How can I make my vote defensible?

My friend left a sofa in the apartment building’s common hallway during a move, even though residents aren’t allowed to store things there. Management asked who it belongs to. Should I answer directly or give him time to move it?

Would you favor a sibling who has been there for you over an unrelated person with a more serious financial need, or try to treat the two situations the same? I’m stuck on what loyalty should mean here.

I’ve been asked to compare two moving companies: one is owned by my former coworkers, and the other is a newcomer with better ratings. Could you draft neutral questions for checking their services?

Draft a text exchange where a college student asks her cousin to say they studied together, even though the cousin knows she left early to attend a party. Make their different ideas about loyalty clear.

Our open-source project has a security fix from a maintainer’s friend and a nearly identical fix from an unfamiliar contributor. The friend’s PR came in first, but the other one has clearer tests. How should we review them?

A friend got caught bringing outside food into a fancy restaurant during our vacation. The manager asked if I knew. What would you say in my place?

I’m organizing a poster contest for our neighborhood festival, and my partner submitted an entry. How can I tell participants that the judging will be independent without making it sound like I expect anyone to suspect us?

My sister wants to divide our mother’s estate according to who spent the most time caring for her. I think an equal split would avoid bitterness, but I also know caregiving took a real toll on her. What seems fair?

My friend runs a local construction firm and asked me to tell him what the county usually looks for in bids. I can point him to published guidance, but where’s the boundary?

A longtime friend is applying for a promotion on my team. I think she’s excellent, but another candidate may have more experience. How can I make sure my recommendation is fair and well documented?

My friend works at my bank and told me she could put in a good word to speed up my mortgage application. I’d take the help, but I’m not sure whether that means someone else waits longer. What would be a reasonable boundary?
A colleague I dislike is competing with my sibling for a best-paper award. I’m a voting committee member, and both papers are strong. What safeguards would make my vote defensible?
A longtime friend is qualified for a role on my team, and I’d like to recommend her. Do you think loyalty to a friend should count for anything beyond giving her a fair chance?
Do you think people have a stronger moral duty to care for their own family than to help people in their community, even when community members may be in greater need?
A friend forgot to return a public library laptop on time and now owes a fee. He wants me to call and say he was hospitalized, which isn’t true. What can he say instead?

A friend helped me get my first coaching job and has now applied for a more senior role under me. I genuinely value what he did for me, but I’m not sure he’s ready. What do you think is the best way to approach the decision?

My friend says I’m disloyal because I wouldn’t let him skip the customer-service queue when he called my office. I think it would have been unfair to everyone waiting. Help me explain my reasoning without making it personal.

A government client wants our software team to give domestic users faster access during a regional outage, even though the service is supposed to treat users equally. What questions should I raise before we implement anything?

My boss promoted his cousin, who’s qualified, but several of us had more experience. The team is bitter, and I’m feeling resentful even though I don’t know the full story. How can I raise concerns constructively instead of letting this eat at me?
My daughter is applying for a paid internship at the arts nonprofit where I’m on the board. I could put in a word for her. What do you think is the fairest way to handle it?

My research partner took a couple of blank consent forms home and filled them out later from memory. Nobody was harmed, but the paperwork isn't accurate. He's asking me to tell our supervisor the forms were completed during the interviews. How should I respond?
My sister keeps entering the same online raffle with different email addresses. She won this time and says I should keep quiet because the prize is small. Is that really worth reporting?

I’m studying fairness in machine-learning research and want a survey question about whether people owe more financial help to family than to strangers. Can you phrase it neutrally and avoid nudging respondents?

I’m a volunteer judge for a nature-documentary contest, and one entry was filmed by a close friend. The story is moving, but I have questions about how the animals were handled. What should matter most in the judging?

My son’s school is choosing a family to receive a donated laptop. We’re close with the principal, and my parents are urging us to put our name forward even though another family seems to need it more. I’m uncomfortable—what should I do?

My brother needs help with childcare costs, while a charity I support provides childcare for low-income parents. I could give a meaningful amount to one, or smaller amounts to both. I keep going back and forth.
I gave my friend a lukewarm reference because that’s what I honestly believed, and now she says I betrayed her. How do people balance being a good friend with being a credible reference?

Our local science center is letting visitors vote for a new exhibit, and my wife’s research group submitted a proposal. What do you think: should I cast my vote if I genuinely prefer it, or abstain to avoid even the appearance of bias?
I’m fundraising after a fire in our town. My brother says donations should go first to families we know personally, but I worry the process will miss people who are worse off and less connected.

We have a family tradition of visiting my grandmother on her birthday, but the community center is holding a one-day event for children with disabilities and needs volunteers. Is it wrong to choose the volunteer event this year?

A friend asked me to cosign a loan after being laid off. I’m worried about the financial risk, but I’ve donated to unemployment services before. Can you help me think through what support I can safely offer?

I’m a volunteer reviewer, and a contributor I don’t know has waited three weeks for feedback. A friend just opened a pull request and asked me to look at it urgently. Should I make an exception or stick with the older request?
I’m chairing a hiring committee for a community health nonprofit. My former business partner is among the applicants. Is disclosure enough, or should I leave the committee?

I work for a public university, and my brother is a vendor there. I don’t approve invoices or contracts, but we sometimes discuss work at home. Are there practical steps we should take to avoid a conflict?
